Hannah — starting point below (broad strokes, will refine into a PDF proposal):

Assumptions:
- Hosted API base: $0.0005 per token (baseline for small volumes)
- Token mix: 70% generation, 30% embeddings/rerank (we need exact split from Oliver)

Suggested tiered discounts (monthly committed tokens):
- Tier A (0–100M): baseline price
- Tier B (100M–500M): 18% discount off baseline
- Tier C (500M–2B): 32% discount off baseline
- Tier D (2B+): custom negotiated (we typically start at 45% and adjust by SLA/commit length)

Burst treatment:
- Burst buffer: customers get 10% monthly free burst credit (unconsumed at month-end does not roll over).
- Short overage (<= 40% above committed tier for <=48 cumulative hours/month): billed at a separate 'burst rate' = baseline * 0.9 (i.e., small premium but cheaper than immediately moving into a higher committed tier).
- If sustained above the committed tier > 48 hours cumulative/month, usage migrates into that month's committed tier pricing for the remaining usage.

Margin / discounts rationale: discounts scale with commitment length (12/24/36 month), and with prevalence of static vs. transient KV cache patterns. If their workloads have predictable KV reuse we can recommend quantization for cost reduction too.

I'll convert to worked numbers once we get the exact Nov split.

- Rishi

Hannah/Rishi — I prepared a worked example and attached the draft proposal PDF (Redwood-EC-proposal-v2.pdf). Worked invoice for the scenario Oliver asked:

Scenario inputs:
- Committed band: 500,000,000 tokens/mo (Tier C entry)
- Baseline price: $0.0005/token
- Tier C discount (500M–2B): 32% -> unit price = $0.00034/token
- Monthly burst credit: 10% of committed = 50,000,000 tokens free for bursts
- Actual usage: 620,000,000 tokens (includes 40M in burst hours)

Calculation:
- Committed covered tokens billed at Tier C: 500,000,000 * $0.00034 = $170,000
- Burst credit applied: 50,000,000 tokens free (covers part of the 40M burst) -> remaining burst charge = 0 tokens (since 40M < 50M)
- Overage (none) -> total = $170,000
- Effective unit price = $170,000 / 620,000,000 = $0.000274

Notes:
- If burst had exceeded credit (say 80M), the excess 30M would be billed at the burst rate: baseline * 0.9 = $0.00045/token -> 30M * $0.00045 = $13,500 extra.
- We can convert the credit to a dollar-denominated safety buffer if Contracts prefers that.

Operational conditions to flag:
- Sustained increases that push them into the next tier for >48 cumulative hours/month will be reclassified and billed at that higher tier for the impacted volume.
- SLA: to guarantee sub-150ms p95 for gen workloads at 500M commit we recommend a reserved Dedicated pool; Hosted can meet latency targets but warm/cold scale characteristics differ.

Attached: Redwood-EC-proposal-v2.pdf (application/pdf) — includes term options (12/24/36 mo), ramp phasing, and suggested SLA credits.

Marissa
